question.prompt: Two adjacent marking lines of an angled parking space are parallel. The perpendicular distance between them (the parking space width) is 2.5 m, and the marking lines form an acute angle of \(30^\circ\) with the driving aisle. How many m of length does each space occupy along the driving aisle?

solutions.explanation: The length \(x\) occupied along the driving aisle satisfies \(2.5=x\cdot\sin30^\circ\), so \(x=2.5\div\frac{1}{2}=5\) m.
solutions.title: Use the sine ratio

solutions.explanation:
Let \(L\) be the aisle length between the two marking lines. Draw a perpendicular from one aisle intersection to the other marking line. The resulting right triangle has hypotenuse \(L\), a \(30^\circ\) angle, and opposite leg \(2.5\) m. Since the leg opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse,
\[
L=2(2.5)=5\text{ m}.
\]
Thus each space occupies \(5\) m along the aisle.
solutions.title: Use the 30° right-triangle property
